title: A non-divergent estimation algorithm in the presence of unknown correlations
summary: The original covariance intersection (CI) paper (American Control Conference 1997). It fuses two estimates whose cross-correlation is unknown by taking a convex combination of their information matrices, which stays consistent whatever the true correlation is. This is the building block behind most decentralized cooperative localization filters that cannot track inter-agent correlations.
key_takeaways: CI gives a consistent fused estimate without knowing cross-covariance
Motivated by decentralized estimation, where a plain Kalman update double-counts shared information
Trades some conservatism for guaranteed consistency

title: Decentralized multi-robot cooperative localization using covariance intersection
summary: IROS 2013 paper applying covariance intersection to multi-robot cooperative localization so that each robot only keeps its own state and covariance. Processing and communication scale linearly with team size, and the authors compare against the earlier split-CI method in simulation and experiments.
key_takeaways: Each robot estimates only its own pose; CI absorbs unknown inter-robot correlations
Linear cost in the number of robots
Standard reference baseline for CI-based cooperative localization

title: Recursive decentralized localization for multi-robot systems with asynchronous pairwise communication
summary: IJRR 37(10) paper describing a fully decentralized EKF for collaborative localization that approximates inter-robot cross-correlations. Only the two robots involved in a relative measurement need to talk, no measurement history is stored, and generic measurement models are supported. Builds on the authors' RSS 2016 paper and is evaluated on real-world datasets.
key_takeaways: Pairwise, asynchronous communication only
Keeps just the latest pose estimate per robot
Approximates cross-correlations instead of dropping them

title: Distributed multirobot localization
summary: IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation 18(5) paper that decomposes the centralized cooperative-localization Kalman filter into one modified filter per robot ('collective localization'). Demonstrated on three robots and compared with a decentralized information filter. A foundational reference for exact (non-CI) distributed cooperative localization.
key_takeaways: Centralized-equivalent estimator split across robots
Cross-correlations are handled exactly, at a communication cost
Shows accuracy gain from relative robot-to-robot measurements

title: Decentralized Localization of Sparsely-Communicating Robot Networks: A Centralized-Equivalent Approach
summary: IEEE T-RO 26(1) paper on decentralized state estimation for robot teams that are not always fully connected. The central result is that a robot can reproduce the centralized estimate using only its own knowledge of the communication history, whenever that estimate is attainable.
key_takeaways: Targets intermittent, sparse communication
Centralized-equivalent result when the information has actually reached the robot
Extended to cooperative SLAM in later work by the same group

title: Cooperative Localization in Wireless Networks
summary: Proceedings of the IEEE 97(2) tutorial on cooperative localization in wireless networks, applied to ultra-wideband ranging. It surveys the approaches and introduces SPAWN, a fully distributed message-passing (factor graph) algorithm with low communication overhead.
key_takeaways: Good tutorial entry point for range-based cooperative positioning
SPAWN: distributed belief propagation over the network
UWB ranging used as the running application

title: A Probabilistic Approach to Collaborative Multi-Robot Localization
summary: Autonomous Robots 8(3) paper extending sample-based Markov (Monte Carlo) localization to robot teams: when one robot detects another, both robots' beliefs are updated. Real-robot and simulation experiments show faster and more accurate global localization than single-robot localization.
key_takeaways: Particle-filter view of cooperative localization
Robot-to-robot detections synchronize beliefs
Handles global localization, not only tracking

title: Cooperative localization for mobile agents: a recursive decentralized algorithm based on Kalman filter decoupling
summary: Published in IEEE Control Systems Magazine 36(2), 2016. Reviews decentralization strategies for cooperative localization with a focus on how each keeps track of inter-agent correlations, then presents a decentralized implementation of the centralized EKF in which agents propagate local intermediate variables instead of cross-covariances, and the agent that takes a relative measurement acts as an interim master for the update.
key_takeaways: Readable survey of CL decentralization strategies
Exact centralized-equivalent EKF without propagating cross-covariances
Open arXiv version

title: Cooperative Localization under Limited Connectivity
summary: IEEE T-RO 35(6) paper with two decentralized cooperative localization algorithms that do not maintain inter-agent correlations: one bounds the joint covariance to stay consistent, the other estimates the unknown cross-covariance by optimization. Only the two agents involved in a relative measurement communicate, with no network-wide connectivity requirement.
key_takeaways: Consistent CL without tracking correlations
Pairwise communication only
Demonstrated in simulation and a robot experiment

title: Resilient and consistent multirobot cooperative localization with covariance intersection
summary: IEEE T-RO 38(1) paper that uses covariance intersection to separate an explicit communication update from the observation update in multirobot cooperative localization, keeping estimates consistent. It analyses when the covariance stays bounded as a function of the communication and observation graphs, and tests resilience on simulated and benchmark physical data.
key_takeaways: Decouples communication from observation so either can fail
Covariance boundedness conditions in terms of graph topology
Directly relevant to lossy tactical links

title: Distributed Visual-Inertial Cooperative Localization
summary: IROS 2021 paper on a consistent distributed visual-inertial estimator for multi-robot cooperative localization. Covariance intersection lets each robot keep only its own state and autocovariance while using common SLAM features and loop closures to other robots' past poses. Validated against a centralized counterpart in simulation and real experiments.
key_takeaways: CI applied to visual-inertial teams, not just range sensors
Uses shared map features and inter-robot loop closures
From the RPNG group behind OpenVINS

title: Weighted Covariance Intersection for Range-based Distributed Cooperative Localization of Multi-Vehicle Systems
summary: Published in IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (2026). Argues that standard CI weighting criteria break down for 3D range-based distributed cooperative localization, where state components differ strongly in scale and observability, and proposes a weighted CI criterion for GNSS-denied multi-vehicle systems.
key_takeaways: Targets 3D range-only cooperative localization
Shows why plug-in CI criteria give unbalanced estimates
Recent (2025-2026) follow-up to the classic CI line

title: Consistent Distributed Cooperative Localization for Ultra Large-Scale Multi-agent Systems
summary: Preprint on cooperative localization for very large networks (the paper's example is satellite mega-constellations) where per-agent resources must not grow with network size. It uses overlapping covariance intersection to exploit limited structure in the cross-correlations while staying consistent, and is fully distributed.
key_takeaways: Per-agent cost independent of team size
Overlapping CI: less conservative than plain CI
Relevant to large drone swarms as well as constellations

title: Autonomous GPS Integrity Monitoring Using the Pseudorange Residual
summary: NAVIGATION 35(2) paper proposing satellite failure detection and isolation from the least-squares pseudorange residual, one of the founding RAIM formulations. Detection uses the range residual test statistic when six or more satellites are in view.
key_takeaways: Residual-based RAIM origin
Detection and isolation from the over-determined solution
Background for every later FDE scheme

title: A Baseline GPS RAIM Scheme and a Note on the Equivalence of Three RAIM Methods
summary: NAVIGATION 39(3) paper written as the RTCA GPS MOPS were released. It proposes a baseline RAIM scheme for performance comparisons and shows that, at equal alarm rates, the range-comparison, least-squares-residual and parity methods give identical results.
key_takeaways: Range comparison, LS residual and parity RAIM are equivalent at equal alarm rate
Intended as a simple standard baseline, not an optimal scheme
Ties RAIM to the aviation MOPS context

title: Solution Separation Versus Residual-Based RAIM
summary: NAVIGATION 61(4) paper with a step-by-step derivation of residual-based and solution-separation RAIM from common integrity and continuity risk definitions, including a parity-space view of solution separation. Solution separation can monitor better because its statistics are tailored to each fault hypothesis, but residual-based RAIM gives tighter integrity bounds in conventional efficient implementations.
key_takeaways: Side-by-side derivation of the two main RAIM families
Parity-space interpretation of solution separation
Useful when choosing an FDE scheme for a fused alt-PNT filter

title: Baseline advanced RAIM user algorithm and possible improvements
summary: IEEE TAES 51(1) description of the baseline multi-fault, multi-constellation ARAIM user algorithm for LPV-200 vertical guidance. It covers pseudorange processing, nominal error models and prior fault probabilities to compute protection levels, how to choose which fault modes to monitor, fault exclusion, and a list of possible improvements.
key_takeaways: The reference ARAIM user algorithm in journal form
Protection levels from solution separation over monitored fault modes
Implemented in Stanford's MAAST tool

title: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C, ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Interim Report (Issue 1.0)
authors: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C - ARAIM Technical Subgroup
summary: First (Milestone 1) report of the EU-US ARAIM subgroup, dated 19 December 2012, prepared by FAA, Stanford, MITRE, IIT, DLR, UniBW Munich, ESA and the European Commission. It gives an ARAIM overview, the requirements analysis for global LPV-200 vertical guidance, a reference user algorithm, first performance evaluation and the identified threats.
key_takeaways: Why ARAIM: multi-constellation integrity with ground-supplied fault rates
LPV-200 as the driving requirement
First reference air algorithm

title: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C-ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Milestone 2 Report
authors: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C - ARAIM Technical Subgroup
summary: Final version dated 11 February 2015. Describes the candidate ARAIM architectures (Horizontal ARAIM and Offline and Online Vertical ARAIM), the Integrity Support Message (ISM) concept that lets a ground system update constellation fault rates and error models, threat allocation, and extended availability results, for comment by the aviation community.
key_takeaways: Horizontal vs offline vs online vertical ARAIM
ISM: ground-provided integrity parameters without avionics changes
Wider URE/SISE and constellation scenarios

title: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C - ARAIM Technical Subgroup - Milestone 3 Report
authors: EU-U.S. Cooperation on Satellite Navigation, Working Group C - ARAIM Technical Subgroup
summary: Final version dated 25 February 2016, concluding the three-phase effort. Adds the proposed ARAIM implementation roadmap, message types for H-ARAIM and for offline and online vertical ARAIM, institutional issues, the relation to SBAS, H-ARAIM availability results and the updated reference user algorithm (Annex A). Also hosted by the European Commission.
key_takeaways: Roadmap toward ARAIM standards
Message definitions per ARAIM mode
Latest reference user algorithm in Annex A

title: Stanford WAAS Laboratory - system metrics (the integrity/availability histogram behind the 'Stanford plot')
summary: Stanford GPS Lab page that explains the 2D histogram of true position error against protection level from its real-time WAAS implementation on the National Satellite Test Bed. It defines the normal-operation, alarm (PL above alert limit) and integrity-failure regions and offers the MATLAB plotting scripts (hplstat.m, vplstat.m). Secondary sources credit the Stanford WAAS lab with this diagram; the page itself is undated.
key_takeaways: Axes: true error (x) vs protection level (y), log-scaled counts
Points with error above PL are integrity failures
Original MATLAB scripts for drawing the plot

title: The Stanford - ESA Integrity Diagram: Focusing on SBAS Integrity
summary: ION GNSS 2006 paper (UPC UPCommons repository record, behind a bot check) that modifies the classical Stanford plot to focus strictly on integrity, since the classical plot is not always conservative for that purpose. Also proposes an 'all-geometries' diagram and reports EGNOS measurement results under this stricter test. The Stanford-ESA diagram became a main integrity assessment tool for EGNOS.
key_takeaways: Stanford-ESA variant is the integrity-conservative version of the Stanford plot
Used for EGNOS safety assessment
Good template for plotting alt-PNT protection levels

title: Navipedia: The Stanford - ESA Integrity Diagram: Focusing on SBAS Integrity
summary: ESA Navipedia article explaining the Stanford plot (position error vs protection level) and its Stanford-ESA modification, including the definitions of misleading and hazardously misleading information used to read the diagram.
key_takeaways: MI: error not bounded by PL while the system is available
HMI: error also exceeds the alert limit
Short open explainer to share with a team

title: GNSS Position Integrity in Urban Environments: A Review of Literature
summary: IEEE T-ITS 19(9) review of GNSS integrity monitoring for urban transport, contrasting it with aviation integrity (multipath, NLOS, different risk definitions) and listing open research issues. Open copy on HAL.
key_takeaways: Why aviation RAIM does not carry over directly to urban ground vehicles
Survey of urban FDE and protection-level methods
Open research problems list

title: Integrity monitoring of Graph-SLAM using GPS and fish-eye camera
summary: NAVIGATION 67(3) paper (journal version of ION GNSS+ 2019 / arXiv 1910.02165) that computes protection levels for a graph-SLAM estimator fusing GPS pseudoranges and fish-eye camera pixel intensities. Vision faults are isolated with a superpixel-based piecewise RANSAC, and protection levels come from worst-case failure slope analysis. Tested in urban and semi-urban driving.
key_takeaways: Multi-fault integrity for joint GPS + vision
Protection levels from failure-slope analysis on linearized graph SLAM
Open arXiv preprint: 1910.02165

title: Integrity of Visual Navigation - Developments, Challenges, and Prospects
summary: Open-access NAVIGATION 69(2) review arguing that the lack of an integrity framework is the main obstacle to using visual navigation in safety-critical roles. It reviews the state of the art and sketches a preliminary integrity description framework for feature-based visual positioning, noting that learning-based methods still lack one.
key_takeaways: Best single review of vision integrity
Proposes how to describe integrity for feature-based VO/VIO
Flags ML-based vision as an open integrity problem

title: Data-Driven Protection Levels for Camera and 3D Map-based Safe Urban Localization
summary: Computes protection levels for localization that matches camera images to a LiDAR-built 3D map, for urban areas where GNSS is unreliable. Position error is modelled as a Gaussian mixture from deep-network data-driven models with outlier weighting, and the PL is found by numerical line search. Submitted to NAVIGATION.
key_takeaways: Protection levels for map-based visual localization, no GNSS
Learned error model plus statistical outlier weighting
Template for PLs on visual geolocalization fixes

title: Safety-Critical LiDAR-Inertial Odometry with On-Manifold Deterministic Protection Level
summary: LiDAR-inertial odometry built on an on-manifold ellipsoidal set-membership filter under an unknown-but-bounded noise assumption. The filter's feasible sets serve as deterministic online protection levels for robot navigation.
key_takeaways: Set-membership (bounded-error) alternative to probabilistic PLs
Closed-form link between point-cloud noise and ICP uncertainty
Online safety bound for LIO

title: Terrain Contour Matching (TERCOM): A Cruise Missile Guidance Aid
summary: Proc. SPIE 0238 paper giving a brief history of TERCOM, how terrain contour matching works (correlating a measured altitude profile against stored elevation data) and its status in 1980. It is the standard English citation for the origin of terrain-correlation navigation; this index uses it only for the navigation-update concept.
key_takeaways: Batch profile correlation against a stored elevation map
Historic baseline that later sequential filters (SITAN, PMF, PF) improved on
Abstract only without SPIE access

title: Nonlinear Kalman filtering techniques for terrain-aided navigation
summary: IEEE TAC 28(3) paper from Sandia (the SITAN line of work) on updating an INS with radar terrain-clearance measurements. It compares an EKF using local terrain slopes, a stochastic linearization fitting a least-squares plane to the terrain, and a bank of parallel reduced-order filters for large initial position uncertainty.
key_takeaways: Sequential (Kalman) terrain aiding, unlike batch TERCOM
Terrain linearization is the core difficulty
Parallel filter bank for acquisition

title: Recursive Bayesian Estimation: Navigation and Tracking Applications
summary: Linkoping University PhD thesis (Dissertation No. 579) on nonlinear, non-Gaussian recursive estimation motivated by terrain-aided aircraft navigation and target tracking. Covers the point-mass filter and particle filters for terrain navigation, compared with the Cramer-Rao bound. A standard English-language TRN reference with free full text.
key_takeaways: Point-mass filter and particle filter for TRN in one place
Cramer-Rao bounds for terrain navigation
Free PDF from Linkoping

title: Terrain navigation using Bayesian statistics
summary: IEEE Control Systems Magazine 19(3) article presenting the point-mass filter for terrain-aided aircraft navigation: a grid approximation of the position density propagated recursively. Monte Carlo and realistic simulations show near-optimal performance across terrain types; the main limit is that cost explodes with state dimension. An open copy is in Linkoping's DiVA.
key_takeaways: The PMF handles arbitrary nonlinearity and noise in low dimension
Density shape tells you estimate quality
Real time for 2D, sometimes 3D

title: Marginalized Particle Filter for Accurate and Reliable Terrain-Aided Navigation
summary: IEEE TAES 45(4) paper integrating INS and terrain-aided positioning in one marginalized (Rao-Blackwellized) particle filter: particles for the nonlinear part, Kalman filters for the conditionally linear part, plus a jointly estimated discrete mode. Simulations reach near Cramer-Rao accuracy. Open copy in Linkoping's DiVA.
key_takeaways: Joint INS + TAP design instead of a separate TRN fix
Marginalized PF keeps the particle count manageable
Handles multimodal terrain via a mode variable

title: Accurate Measurement Calculation Method for Interferometric Radar Altimeter-Based Terrain Referenced Navigation
summary: Open-access Sensors paper on TRN with an interferometric radar altimeter, which outputs slant range and cross-track look angle to the closest terrain point. It derives a formula for that point's 3D relative position using angle of attack and sideslip instead of Euler angles, checks it on real flight data, and shows in TRN simulation that wind otherwise biases the result.
key_takeaways: Interferometric altimeters give range plus look angle, not just height
Wind (alpha/beta) matters for the measurement model
Real flight data used for validation

title: Ant-Mutated Immune Particle Filter Design for Terrain Referenced Navigation with Interferometric Radar Altimeter
summary: Open-access Remote Sensing paper proposing a particle filter variant (ant-colony mutation inside an immune auxiliary particle filter) to cope with low-grade interferometric radar altimeter errors in TRN. Evaluated by Monte Carlo TRN simulation on a UAV.
key_takeaways: Targets low-cost IRA measurement errors
Particle diversity management for TRN
Simulation-only evaluation

title: Design of Efficient Point-Mass Filter with Application in Terrain Aided Navigation
summary: FUSION 2023 paper on speeding up the time-update (prediction) step of the grid-based point-mass filter for models with linear dynamics, unifying continuous and discrete formulations. The authors report large time-complexity reductions without accuracy loss in a terrain-aided navigation example, and release MATLAB code.
key_takeaways: Makes the PMF cheap enough for real-time TAN
MATLAB code on GitHub
Good modern successor to Bergman's PMF

title: Tensor Decompositions for Online Grid-Based Terrain-Aided Navigation
summary: Preprint (in review for FUSION 2026) that scales grid-based filters to higher state dimensions with a Lagrangian time update and low-rank tensor decompositions, exploiting block-diagonal dynamics and sparsely coupled measurements. Demonstrated on terrain-aided navigation, with reproducible MATLAB code.
key_takeaways: Pushes grid filters beyond 2-3 dimensions
Fully reproducible experiments
Code: pesslovany/Matlab-LagrangianPMF

title: Contours-Seeking Proposal Density Particle Filter and Resilient Terrain-Referenced Navigation
summary: Author's accepted version of an IEEE TAES 61(6) (Dec 2025) paper. Proposes a particle-filter proposal that nudges particles along terrain slopes toward the most probable terrain contours (Gaussian mixture random forcing plus auxiliary sampling) to fight degeneracy under multimodal likelihoods and unknown prediction bias.
key_takeaways: Addresses PF degeneracy, the classic TRN failure mode
Robust to unknown INS bias and multimodal noise
Simulation study

title: Terrain-Aided Navigation Without Raycasting: A Sliding Grid Approach for Point Cloud Processing
summary: Compares two DEM-based measurement models for point-cloud (lidar-style) terrain-aided INS: classic ray casting versus a 'sliding grid' that needs no ray casting. The sliding grid gives comparable accuracy, especially at higher altitude, at much lower compute, targeting embedded hardware.
key_takeaways: Point-cloud TAN beyond a single altimeter beam
Avoids GPU-hungry ray casting
Relevant to scanning lidar or radar altimeters

title: Vision-Based Terrain Relative Navigation on High-Altitude Balloon and Sub-Orbital Rocket
summary: AIAA SciTech 2023 paper evaluating camera-based TRN that matches landmarks from a satellite image database and uses inertial data between frames. Tested on a World View high-altitude balloon descending from 33 km and on Blue Origin New Shepard NS-23 camera data, with robustness to fast rotation and cloud obstruction.
key_takeaways: Real flight data, not simulation
Visual TRN across a large altitude range
Draper/MIT work

title: Advanced Aeromagnetic Compensation Models for Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
summary: MIT AeroAstro PhD thesis (advisor Alan Edelman) on removing the aircraft's own magnetic field so magnetic anomaly maps can be used for navigation. It studies four groups of methods: linear compensation, nonlinear (neural) compensation, online compensation and covariance-adaptive filtering. The models are implemented in MagNav.jl. DSpace terms: in copyright, educational use permitted.
key_takeaways: The full technical background behind MagNav.jl
Compares Tolles-Lawson, neural and online compensation
Free PDF on DSpace@MIT

title: Derivation and Extensions of the Tolles-Lawson Model for Aeromagnetic Compensation
summary: Short open reference note that re-derives the Tolles-Lawson aircraft magnetic field model (permanent, induced and eddy-current terms), states where the assumptions enter, describes the calibration procedure, and adds a second-order correction and a way to build the vector aircraft field.
key_takeaways: Clear derivation of the standard compensation model
Explains the calibration-box flight
Pairs with the MagNav challenge data

title: Absolute Positioning Using the Earth's Magnetic Anomaly Field
summary: NAVIGATION 63(2) journal paper: a particle-filter framework that aids an aircraft INS with optically pumped cesium magnetometer measurements compared against an anomaly map, while estimating the temporal variations of the field. Analyses altitude and magnetic-storm dependence with flight-test and observatory data. The article is a U.S. Government work, public domain in the USA; the related AFIT dissertation is freely available.
key_takeaways: Particle filter on scalar anomaly measurements
Models temporal (diurnal/storm) field variation
Public-domain US Government work

title: Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation
summary: IEEE TAES 53(1) paper describing a passive airborne navigation system (scalar magnetometer, INS, barometer, anomaly map) with a particle filter and a full measurement equation linking magnetometer readings to the map. Flight-tested over Louisa, Virginia; the authors call the reported accuracy a best case under ideal conditions.
key_takeaways: First flight-test validation of the AFIT MagNav filter
Complete measurement equation
Best-case result, survey aircraft conditions

title: Magnetic Navigation on an F-16 Aircraft Using Online Calibration
summary: IEEE TAES 58(1) paper on magnetic anomaly navigation flown on an F-16, where the platform's magnetic interference is far larger than on survey aircraft and drifts. A combined batch and online calibration gives better accuracy than batch-only calibration on 1.5-hour flights.
key_takeaways: Operational fighter platform, not a quiet survey aircraft
Online calibration needed for drifting platform fields
Key evidence for MagNav on military aircraft

title: Airborne Magnetic Anomaly Navigation with Neural-Network-Augmented Online Calibration
summary: Published in the Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics (2026). A 'cold-start' MagNav EKF that estimates kinematic states, Tolles-Lawson coefficients and the weights of a residual neural network in flight, so no calibration flight or pre-training is needed. Validated on the MagNav Challenge dataset.
key_takeaways: No prior calibration flight
EKF update equivalent to online natural-gradient training
Physics model first, NN only for residuals

title: Acquisition, Doppler Tracking, and Positioning With Starlink LEO Satellites: First Results
summary: IEEE TAES 58(3) letter with the first acquisition, Doppler tracking and positioning results from Starlink downlinks without knowing the signal structure: a generalized-likelihood-ratio acquisition test and a Kalman-filter Doppler tracker, with six satellites tracked.
key_takeaways: Blind acquisition of undisclosed Starlink signals
Doppler-only positioning works with a handful of satellites
Received the IEEE M. Barry Carlton Award

title: Unveiling Starlink LEO Satellite OFDM-Like Signal Structure Enabling Precise Positioning
summary: IEEE TAES 60(2) letter that estimates the structure of Starlink's OFDM-like reference signals and frame length, and proposes a blind receiver that acquires multiple satellites, estimates their reference signals and Doppler, and tracks carrier and code phase. Of six tracked satellites, three sent pure tones and three OFDM-like signals.
key_takeaways: Blind reference-signal estimation
Carrier and code phase from Starlink
Bridges pure-tone Doppler to OFDM ranging

title: Unveiling Starlink for PNT
summary: Open-access NAVIGATION 72(1) paper describing the full Starlink OFDM beacon via blind beacon estimation, the processing gain this gives over previously published sequences, achievable C/N0 for different reception setups, and the first carrier phase, Doppler and code phase observables from Starlink OFDM. Uses signal collections from 2021 to 2024 and notes step-like corrections that contaminate OFDM observables. Won the ION Samuel Burka Award.
key_takeaways: Full beacon gives large processing gain for low-gain antennas
Pilot-tone vs OFDM observable quality compared
Open access, with an ION webinar companion

title: Fused Low-Earth-Orbit GNSS
summary: Accepted to IEEE TAES. Proposes 'fused LEO GNSS': a cooperative PNT service hosted on a broadband mega-constellation's own transmitters, clocks and spectrum. Assesses the opportunity cost to the operator in time-space-bandwidth product and energy, concluding that a near-instantaneous-fix service would cost a small fraction of Starlink downlink capacity.
key_takeaways: Cooperative (operator-supported) LEO PNT vs opportunistic use
Opportunity-cost argument in downlink capacity
Foundation for the UT group's LEO PNT work

title: Timing Properties of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
summary: IEEE TAES 62 (2026) paper characterizing Starlink frame timing for pseudorange-based opportunistic PNT. It finds ns-level jitter periods (good) but also abrupt timing adjustments, episodic high-jitter periods and only loose disciplining to GPS time, which the authors judge incompatible with GPS-like PNT unless corrected, and attribute to software choices.
key_takeaways: Starlink frame timing is disciplined to GPS time only loosely
Abrupt per-second timing jumps on v1.0/v1.5 satellites
Third-party corrections could fix it

title: Pilots and Other Predictable Elements of the Starlink Ku-Band Downlink
summary: Identifies dedicated edge-pilot symbols and other predictable elements in the Starlink Ku-band waveform, publishes the edge-pilot sequences, and shows most QPSK symbols follow a regular template rather than carrying user data. Exploiting these elements gives a large processing gain so compact low-gain receivers can get precise time of arrival even from side beams.
key_takeaways: Explicit Starlink pilot sequences disclosed
Predictable frame content enables TOA with small antennas
UT Austin with Psiaki (Virginia Tech)

title: OFDM-Based Positioning with Unknown Data Payloads: Bounds and Applications to LEO PNT
summary: Derives the Ziv-Zakai bound on time-of-arrival estimation for OFDM signals with both known pilots and unknown data, capturing low-SNR threshold effects that Cramer-Rao bounds miss. Evaluates maximum-likelihood and decision-directed estimators on simulated LEO non-terrestrial-network channels.
key_takeaways: Unknown payload symbols still carry ranging information
ZZB vs CRB at low SNR
Theory for opportunistic OFDM ranging

title: LEO-PNT With Starlink: Development of a Burst Detection Algorithm Based on Signal Measurements
summary: Measures Starlink signals and builds a correlation-based burst detector, then measures burst carrier frequency (Doppler) and estimates attainable positioning accuracy. The authors argue it works with an omnidirectional antenna in an operationally relevant setup.
key_takeaways: Burst detection as the first step of Doppler positioning
Omnidirectional antenna, no dish
European (UniBw Munich) LEO-PNT work

title: Clock-Shift-Aided Blind Doppler Matching in Passive SDR Monitoring Data for LEO Doppler Positioning
summary: Associates unlabeled Doppler traces in passive SDR spectrum-monitoring scans (no raw IQ) with TLE-predicted Starlink/OneWeb satellites, using slope-consistent segments, a clock-offset search and multi-metric matching, then runs batch Doppler positioning on open UK monitoring data. Submitted to IEEE NAVICON 2026.
key_takeaways: Positioning from spectrum waterfalls, not IQ samples
Receiver clock offset search is the key step
Uses open monitoring data

title: Broadband LEO Constellations for Navigation
summary: NAVIGATION 65(2) paper analysing how broadband LEO mega-constellations could provide navigation: stronger signals against jamming, much better satellite geometry from sheer numbers, which lets the signal-in-space range error be relaxed, and a benign radiation environment that allows COTS payloads.
key_takeaways: Early quantitative case for LEO PNT
Geometry gain offsets worse clocks and orbits

title: Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) Through Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites: A Survey on Current Status, Challenges, and Opportunities
summary: Open-access IEEE Access survey of LEO-PNT: system design steps and challenges, candidate physical-layer parameters, design tools and simulators, satellite-ground channel models, and commercial prospects, written by a multidisciplinary Finnish-led team.
key_takeaways: Broad map of the LEO-PNT design space
Lists simulators and channel models
Good starting reading for a LEO-PNT hackathon track

title: GNSS Timing Spoofing Detection: Methods and Analysis using Jammertest data
summary: University of Vaasa master's thesis (supervised by Heidi Kuusniemi) analysing u-blox ZED-F9P data from a Jammertest 2024 timing-spoofing event. C/N0 monitoring was ineffective; pseudorange RMS and NMEA validity flags caught anomalies with false positives; an Isolation Forest model detected the spoofing with very few false alarms. Recommends validity flags as a trigger plus ML verification. The repository page sits behind a bot check.
key_takeaways: Uses real live-spoofing data, not simulation
C/N0 alone does not reveal timing spoofing
Cheap receiver-side detection recipe

title: Empirical Evaluation of GNSS Timing Spoofing and Detection Using Machine Learning
summary: IPIN 2025 paper on timing spoofing detection with Jammertest 2024 data. Position parameters were compromised at lower spoofing power than timing parameters, which could give early warning; NMEA validity flags detected much but not all of the attack; an unsupervised Isolation Forest closed the gap. Self-archived copies exist in the Vaasa and Tampere repositories.
key_takeaways: Position degrades before time: use it as an early warning
Unsupervised detector, no labelled spoofing needed
Targets critical-infrastructure timing receivers

title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Framework for Zero-Day Time-Push GNSS Spoofing Detection
summary: Preprint on detecting time-push spoofing against static GNSS receivers with an autoencoder (hybrid quantum-classical) trained only on authentic tracking-stage features, so it can flag unseen attack types. Compared with classical autoencoders and supervised models across simplistic, intermediate and sophisticated time-push scenarios.
key_takeaways: Anomaly detection trained on clean data only
Focus on time-push attacks on static timing receivers
Quantum part is optional for a hackathon; the classical baseline is the useful bit

title: MILUV: A Multi-UAV Indoor Localization dataset with UWB and Vision
summary: Multi-UAV indoor dataset (three quadcopters, 36 experiments) with UWB ranging including raw timestamps, channel impulse response and inter-robot ranges, stereo and downward cameras, IMU, laser height, magnetometer and motion-capture ground truth, in LOS and NLOS. Data on Figshare+ under CC BY 4.0; the devkit (decargroup/miluv) is MIT. Paper: arXiv 2504.14376.
key_takeaways: CC BY 4.0 data, MIT devkit
Inter-robot UWB for cooperative localization tests
CIR data for NLOS classification

title: Addressing Relative Pose Impact on UWB Localization: Dataset Introduction and Analysis
summary: Short paper introducing a drone UWB dataset that isolates how the relative pose between UWB devices affects ranging: six flight sequences with two-way ranging to four anchors, a stereo VIO setup, and motion-capture ground truth for both the drone and the anchors. Data in the cjhhalla/RCV_uwb_dataset GitHub repo (rosbags on Google Drive), which has no licence file, so reuse terms are unstated.
key_takeaways: Characterizes antenna-orientation effects on UWB range error
Useful for building a realistic UWB noise model
No explicit licence

title: UWB-based system for UAV Localization in GNSS-Denied Environments: Characterization and Dataset
summary: IROS 2020 paper characterizing a low-cost, portable Decawave DWM1001 UWB system for indoor UAV flight, including anchor placement, altitude and speed effects and anchor self-calibration, with open data and methods. Data in the TIERS/uwb-drone-dataset GitHub repo, which has no licence file.
key_takeaways: Cheap DWM1001 hardware, movable anchors
Accuracy vs anchor geometry and altitude
No explicit licence

title: GSV-Cities: Toward Appropriate Supervised Visual Place Recognition
summary: Neurocomputing 2022 paper introducing GSV-Cities, a street-level training set covering 40+ cities over 14 years with accurate place labels, and a study of metric-learning losses for VPR training. It is the training set used by MixVPR, BoQ and several later methods. Licence: the Kaggle dataset is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (non-commercial, no derivatives); the GitHub code repo has no licence file.
key_takeaways: Standard training set for modern VPR
CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: research use only
Hosted on Kaggle

title: Rethinking Visual Geo-localization for Large-Scale Applications
summary: CVPR 2022 paper introducing San Francisco eXtra Large (SF-XL), a city-wide geo-localization dataset, and CosPlace, which casts VPR training as classification to avoid expensive negative mining. SF-XL is obtained through a request form that states it is 'publicly available for research purposes'; no formal licence is given. The CosPlace code is MIT.
key_takeaways: Classification training scales to city-size data
SF-XL access via form, research use
CosPlace code: MIT

title: EigenPlaces: Training Viewpoint Robust Models for Visual Place Recognition
summary: ICCV 2023 paper that clusters training data to show the network the same points of interest from different viewpoints, building viewpoint robustness into global descriptors without extra supervision. Trained on SF-XL.
key_takeaways: Viewpoint robustness, relevant to oblique aerial views
No extra labels needed
MIT-licensed code

title: MixVPR: Feature Mixing for Visual Place Recognition
summary: WACV 2023 paper proposing a holistic aggregation that mixes backbone feature maps through a cascade of feature-mixing blocks instead of NetVLAD-style local aggregation, aiming at accuracy with low latency. Trained on GSV-Cities.
key_takeaways: Simple, fast global descriptor
Trained on GSV-Cities
Good baseline for onboard VPR

title: Deep Visual Geo-localization Benchmark
summary: CVPR 2022 oral presenting an open framework to build, train and test visual geo-localization pipelines with swappable backbones, aggregation and negative mining, plus a large experimental study of how each choice affects recall, runtime and memory.
key_takeaways: Systematic guide to VPR design choices
Common evaluation protocol
MIT-licensed framework

title: VPAIR - Aerial Visual Place Recognition and Localization in Large-scale Outdoor Environments
summary: ICRA 2022 aerial-robotics workshop paper introducing VPAIR: downward camera images from a light aircraft flying above 300 m, each paired with a reference render with depth and a 6-DoF pose, over 100+ km of urban, farmland and forest terrain. Licence: the README says academic use only, commercial use prohibited (the small Zenodo sample is tagged CC BY 4.0).
key_takeaways: Medium-altitude aerial VPR benchmark
Reference renders with depth
Academic use only

title: ALTO: A Large-Scale Dataset for UAV Visual Place Recognition and Localization
summary: Helicopter-flown aerial dataset over Ohio and Pennsylvania (two long trajectories) with GPS-INS ground truth, accelerometer, laser altimeter and downward RGB imagery, plus reference imagery for VPR benchmarking. The MetaSLAM/ALTO repo is BSD-3-Clause; no separate data licence is stated.
key_takeaways: Long-range aerial VPR and registration benchmark
Includes laser altimeter (TRN-adjacent)
Repo BSD-3-Clause

title: Visual place recognition for aerial imagery: A survey
summary: Robotics and Autonomous Systems 183 (2025) survey and evaluation methodology for VPR on aerial imagery. Benchmarks several VPR methods and shows that the zoom level and overlap chosen when cutting satellite map tiles strongly affect results. Code in prime-slam/aero-vloc.
key_takeaways: How to tile satellite maps for VPR matters
Hands-on benchmark with code
Directly useful for drone-to-satellite geolocalization

title: Visual Place Recognition for Large-Scale UAV Applications
summary: Introduces LASED, a large aerial VPR training set of about a million images from 170,000 locations across Estonia sampled over a decade, and uses steerable (rotation-equivariant) CNNs to handle the heading ambiguity of nadir UAV images.
key_takeaways: Multi-year aerial imagery for cross-season training
Rotation-equivariant networks for unknown heading
Aerial counterpart to GSV-Cities

title: Are State-of-the-art Visual Place Recognition Techniques any Good for Aerial Robotics?
summary: Early benchmark of eight ground-robot VPR techniques on two aerial place-recognition datasets, comparing matching performance, processing power and memory, and laying out why aerial VPR differs (viewpoint change, payload-limited compute).
key_takeaways: Ground VPR does not transfer directly to aerial
Compute and memory as first-class metrics
Good framing for an onboard VPR budget
